title: Archetypes
hook: Answer a short original questionnaire, pick one of the avatars it offers, and roleplay an archetype rather than a named character.
proposed_defaults_note: players, minutes and complexity are PROPOSALS; the owner has not decided them
theme: personality archetypes (original; no MBTI or 16Personalities material)

open_questions.question: Format
options: Card deck plus one-page questionnaire sheet

open_questions.question: GM or GM-less
options: GM-less, table frames scenes in turn

open_questions.question: How many avatars the results offer
options: Three: best match, near neighbour, stretch opposite

open_questions.question: What the archetype changes in play
options: Drive, signature move and blind spot; token for acting in type
open_questions.recommendation: Drive, signature move, blind spot plus in-type token

testing_note: Role-playing game: simulation can test questionnaire reachability and balance of the 16 outcomes, avatar-offer rules, token economy and scene length; it cannot test roleplay fun, question fairness or table dynamics. Human sessions required.

comparables.name: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
comparables.difference: Video game, moral-dilemma questions give one forced class; this offers several avatars and is tabletop.

comparables.name: Fiasco
comparables.difference: GM-less improv from a pick-a-playbook menu; this starts from a questionnaire and archetypes.

comparables.name: Emotional Intelligence (personality deduction party game)
comparables.difference: Guessing traits about players; this is roleplay of a type.
